packages.name: iBoot32Patcher
packages.checksum_source: SHA-256 calculated from this GitHub archive on 2026-09-28. LukeZGD's fork (the one Legacy-iOS-Kit ships), master of 2026-09-14. firmwarekit runs it as a separate process (K48IBoot.patchIBoot) for the k48 iboot recipe. Built with build-support/patches/iBoot32Patcher-ltm.patch (word-aligned xref matches only, smoke #48); K48IBootTests checks its output byte-for-byte against the Legacy-iOS-Kit v25.09.01 binary on every k48 build that binary patches.

packages.name: ANGLE

packages.name: swift-binary-parsing
packages.checksum_source: SHA-256 calculated from this GitHub archive on 2026-10-21. Pinned exact in Packages/FirmwareKit/Package.swift and Packages/LightTouchCore/Package.swift. FirmwareKit's readers of firmware files (HFSPlus, BTreeFile, UDIFReader, TarArchive) and LightTouchCore's reads of guest and media bytes (MediaIdentity, MediaSong, StatusBarOverride) parse through its ParserSpan, whose reads check their bounds and throw. Its macro target builds swift-syntax (the next record: build time only), so xcodebuild runs with -skipMacroValidation; its RawSpan needs the toolchain's libswiftCompatibilitySpan.dylib below macOS 26, which the app embeds in Frameworks.

packages.name: swift-syntax
packages.checksum_source: SHA-256 calculated from this GitHub archive on 2026-10-21. Build time only: swift-binary-parsing's macro target takes it (from 603.0.0, so SwiftPM resolves the 603 releases, not 604; Package.resolved pins the version), and SwiftPM uses its prebuilt MacroSupport where the toolchain has one. The macro runs in the compiler; nothing of swift-syntax is linked or ships, so scripts/vendor (SwiftPackageLinks) copies no license of it and records it in build-inputs.json's swift_packages_unlinked.

packages.name: swift-crypto
packages.checksum_source: SHA-256 calculated from this GitHub archive on 2026-10-20. Pinned exact in Packages/FirmwareKit/Package.swift and Packages/LightTouchCore/Package.swift. Crypto (CryptoKit itself on Apple platforms) for digests and HMAC; CryptoExtras (BoringSSL) for FirmwareKit's AES-CBC only off Apple platforms, where there is no CommonCrypto: BoringSSL's error macros put each C source's absolute build path into the binary, which the release check refuses. Never in LightTouchDevice, which loads the GPL-2.0-only emulator: DeviceRuntime and HostRuntime keep Security and CryptoKit.
